channel.title: WireShaman
channel.description: Cybersecurity and technology intelligence: what's actually breaking, how it works, and what to do about it.

item.title: Google's Gemini 4 Argon lands in limited release — and retakes the frontier benchmarks lead
item.dc:creator: By the ADS News technology desk
item.description: Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Argon targets long-horizon software engineering, enterprise knowledge work and defensive cybersecurity. It opens at half its standard price, is gated to trusted cyber defenders first, and scores level with GPT-6 Astra on independent intelligence index.

item.title: Microsoft's Azure Maia 300 targets cloud AI inference
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Wire
item.description: Microsoft announced its third-generation Maia AI chip, built to deliver up to 40 percent more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems.

item.title: The TLS 1.3 handshake: why secure connections got faster and more private
item.dc:creator: By the ADS News technology desk
item.description: TLS 1.3, finalized in 2018, cut the secure handshake from two round trips to one, made forward secrecy mandatory, and dropped insecure legacy ciphers such as RC4 and static RSA.

item.title: Meta ships its first frontier model with Muse Wonder, betting on agents and active memory
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: Meta Superintelligence Labs has released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, its first frontier model pair, with agentic tool calling, active memory, and a cheaper per-token price than its rivals.

item.title: Kaspersky says Android attackers are shifting to app-store loaders as on-device malware falls
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: Kaspersky's Q2 2026 mobile threat report found 1.99 million mobile malware attacks and a pivot toward dropper-based banking Trojans delivered through Google Play.

item.title: Ledger Nano X spy-chip implant steals recovery phrases pixel by pixel
item.dc:creator: AdsNews Desk
item.description: Tibane Labs and Grand Idea Studio document a tampered Ledger Nano X with a soldered-on second computer and cellular modem that captures the on-screen 24-word seed and exfiltrates it while passing genuine-device checks.

item.title: How JWT tokens work: the three-part string behind most logins
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: A JSON Web Token is a compact, signed string — header, payload, signature — that lets a server trust a request without keeping a session. Here is what each part does and where it leaks.

item.title: Attacker Chains Three Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days for Root Access — Only Two Are Patched
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: Volexity says attacker UTA0576 broke through a fully patched Ivanti Connect Secure appliance via a triple zero-day chain, stealing LDAP and Active Directory credentials while evading the Integrity Checker Tool.

item.title: Linus Torvalds Wrote an Experimental Linux Kernel Series With Claude Code
item.dc:creator: Wireshaman Editorial Desk
item.description: Torvalds pushed an eight-patch noref-filemap branch that triples small-read throughput on his laptop and credits Anthropic Claude Code with the code, tests, and review draft.

item.title: What Is DRAM? The Memory Your Computer Runs On, Explained
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Editorial
item.description: DRAM is the RAM in your computer. It stores each bit in a tiny capacitor held by one transistor, and it leaks, so it must be refreshed. Here is how it works and why it matters.

item.title: NVIDIA Reports a 24 GB RTX 5080 for Early 2027 as the RTX 5090 Fades From the Roadmap
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Editorial
item.description: A new 24 GB RTX 5080 is reportedly slated for Q1 2027 after NVIDIA begins winding down RTX 5090 production. What is verified and what is not.

item.title: Microsoft Unveils Decision-1, a New Thinking Model Built to Make Fast Decisions
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Editorial
item.description: Microsoft launched Decision-1, a new model that scores options and judges the next move instead of generating long text, alongside faster transcription and video models.

item.title: Docker Hub’s GhostPat Flaw Let One User Push Images as Another — For Two Years
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Editorial
item.description: Docker fixed a critical Docker Hub flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-105445, that let any user transfer a personal access token to another account and act as that user in the registry.

item.title: The RAM crisis has no end in sight: DDR4 prices jumped 24% in a quarter and even the old standard is now scarce
item.dc:creator: The WireShaman Editors
item.description: Memory is getting pricier than ever. DDR4 is up roughly 24% in a single quarter, and Intel's CEO says consumers face one to three more years of the AI-driven shortage.

item.title: Mistral launches Large 4 (Le Chonk), a 1-trillion-parameter open-weight model
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Newsroom
item.description: Mistral unveiled Mistral Large 4, a natively multimodal 1T-parameter MoE model with 52B active parameters, now in public preview on Mistral Studio with open weights due at the end of the month.

item.title: GitLab fixes critical remote-code-execution flaw (CVE-2026-97229) in versions 19.4.2, 19.3.4 and 19.2.8
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Newsroom
item.description: GitLab shipped a critical patch set on 12 October 2026 that closes an unauthenticated remote-code-execution bug in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler alongside 23 other issues.

item.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-6 with Intelligent UI: answers that build calculators, charts and interactive tools
item.dc:creator: The WireShaman Desk
item.description: OpenAI began rolling out GPT-6 in ChatGPT on October 7, 2026, paired with a new capability called Intelligent UI that lets the model answer questions with charts, calculators, forms and interactive tools built on the spot.

item.title: Windows 11 24H2 and Windows 10 LTSB 2016 just hit end of updates — here's what you should do now
item.dc:creator: WireShaman editorial team
item.description: Microsoft's October 2026 security release is the final update for Windows 11 24H2 (Home and Pro) and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB 2016. The last patch also flips the Active Directory Federation Services Distributed Key Manager container ACL hardening into Enforcement mode.

item.title: Microsoft and Nvidia unveil the Surface Laptop Ultra and the RTX Spark superchip
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra ships on the new Nvidia RTX Spark superchip, starting at $2,600, alongside a $6,000 Dev Box workstation and a revamped Windows 11 built to run AI locally.

item.title: Anthropic unveils the 'Cyber Mission' and a free AI scanner for open-source software
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Research Desk
item.description: Anthropic launched a new long-term 'Cyber Mission' built around a free OSS Scanner that runs its strongest models over open-source projects, a Critical Infrastructure Defense Program backed by major security firms, and an expanded Cyber Verification Program that opens its most capable models to more defenders.

item.title: Police Shutter KillSec Ransomware and Arrest a 16-Year-Old Suspected Operator
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: A coordinated European operation seized the KillSec ransomware infrastructure and identified a teenage suspect alleged to have run the group's attack campaign.

item.title: “Midnight Mimosa”: Cheap Android Phones Ship With Malware You Can’t Uninstall
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: A new preinstalled firmware-root malware named Midnight Mimosa was found on low-cost MediaTek Android phones sold across more than 150 countries, enabling ad fraud and turning victims into residential proxies.

item.title: FBI Arrests Canadian Ransomware Negotiator in ShinyHunters Crackdown
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: A 54-year-old Canadian cybersecurity executive who helps victims negotiate ransomware extortion was arrested in Pennsylvania and moved to the Eastern District of Texas, the center of the FBI's ShinyHunters investigation.

item.title: Pwn2Own Ireland 2026: Researchers Remotely Crack the Pixel 10 Three Times
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 ended with a record payout, and the Google Pixel 10 drew the largest single share after three teams each proved remote, unpatched exploits.

item.title: MediaTek's October 2026 bulletin silences 31 flaws, led by two critical modem bugs
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Research Desk
item.description: MediaTek's October 2026 security bulletin addresses 31 chipset vulnerabilities, including two critical out-of-bounds write flaws in its modem stack that can be triggered from a rogue base station with no user interaction.

item.title: Microsoft Debuts Maia 300 Chip and Pledges Multi-Gigawatt Inference Fleet
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: Microsoft's third-generation Maia 300 AI accelerator, unveiled on 12 October 2026, is aimed squarely at AI inference and is planned for multi-gigawatt Azure deployments beginning in 2027.

item.title: What Is OAuth? Authorization, Tokens and PKCE Explained
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: OAuth lets an application receive limited access to another service without receiving the user's password. Here is how roles, tokens, scopes and PKCE fit together.

item.title: AMD's 192GB Ryzen AI Halo Pushes Local AI Beyond Laptop Memory Limits
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: AMD's new Ryzen AI Halo developer platform combines a Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 with up to 192GB of unified memory for large local AI workloads.

item.title: OnePlus 16 Launches in China: 3,840Hz “Oriental” LTPO Display, 200MP Camera, 9,000mAh Battery
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: OnePlus announced the OnePlus 16 in China on October 12, headlined by its 4th Gen Oriental display, Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, and 9,000mAh battery. What we know, what is confirmed, and what is still unverified.

item.title: CISA Warns of Active Zero-Day Exploits in Citrix NetScaler — New CVE Added
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: CISA expanded its Citrix NetScaler alert on October 9, adding CVE-2026-107406 and clarifying the relationship between two more CVEs. Patch the full set and review your compromise-response posture.

item.title: What Is a TLS Handshake? How HTTPS Proves It’s Safe to Talk
item.description: A plain-English walkthrough of the TLS handshake — ClientHello to Finished, and what RFC 8446 (TLS 1.3) actually changed in 2018. Why it matters, step by step, no jargon.

item.title: Nvidia RTX Spark Laptops Arrive October 16: Surface Laptop Ultra, Full Lineup with Specs and Pricing
item.description: Nvidia's RTX Spark superchip goes on sale across six brands starting October 16, 2026. Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,599, the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box at $5,999.99. Here's every model, price, and what the unified-memory Arm chip actually changes.

item.title: FIPS 140-2 Sunsetting Sept 21 2026: What "Historical" Status Means for Your Stack
item.description: On September 21, 2026, every remaining active FIPS 140-2 certificate moves to the NIST Historical list. A procurement change, not a vulnerability. Here's what to verify in your security stack.

item.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Auth Bypass (CVE-2026-76504) Explained
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Cisco’s out-of-band advisory confirms active exploitation of a critical, unauthenticated authentication bypass in the Catalyst SD-WAN Manager API (CVE-2026-76504, CVSS 9.8, added to CISA KEV). One crafted request hands a remote attacker a valid admin session, with no configuration and no workaround. Here’s what’s exposed, what’s patched, and what to do now.

item.title: ASOS Data Breach: Customer Details, Search History and a “Snowflake” Access Claim
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Employees of the online fashion retailer ASOS were social-engineered and customer records were leaked, including names, contact details, and search-history terms. Researchers estimate 2–5 million customers affected. Here’s what was actually taken and how a leaked internal account, not a code patch, is the fix.

item.title: Android October 2026 Security Update Ships 25 Vulnerability Fixes Across 7 Critical CVEs
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Google’s October 2026 Android Security Bulletin (patch level 2026-10-01) covers 25 CVEs across the Android Open Source Project, of which 7 are Critical. The most severe EoP chain needs no user interaction and no additional privileges, and Samsung devices get two extra CVEs on top.

item.title: Nvidia RTX Spark N1X Hits the Dell XPS 16: 128 GB of Unified Memory, 1 PetaFLOP FP4
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Dell’s XPS 16 Creator Edition (DX16263) is the first laptop built around Nvidia’s new N1X: a 20-core Grace CPU plus 6,144-CUDA-core Blackwell GPU sharing 128 GB of unified LPDDR5X, hitting 1 petaFLOP FP4, arriving October 16 at $3,799.99. It’s a Mac Studio in a laptop and Windows ARM’s best excuse, at once.

item.title: Anthropic Ships Claude Sonnet 5.5: Sonnet-Level Speed, Opus-Level Coding, Half the Price
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Released September 28, 2026, Claude Sonnet 5.5 lands at $2/$10 per million tokens, roughly 50% lower unit cost than Opus 5.5 at the same performance level, and runs ~30% faster than Sonnet 5. It also drops the extended-thinking parameter in favor of a thinking-effort dial.

item.title: P7 DarkSword: The iOS Exploit Kit Built to Steal Your Crypto Wallet and Remote-Control Your Phone
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Researchers from PARS Defense, iVerify, and Lookout have detailed an enhanced iOS exploit kit that targets iOS 18.4 through 18.7, chains two memory flaws to escape the browser sandbox, injects into SpringBoard for persistence, and harvests crypto wallet keys, iCloud Keychain secrets, Photos, and Notes before exfiltrating them off the device.

item.title: Why So Much Traffic Uses AES-GCM — and What Its Authentication Tag Proves
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: AES-GCM is the cipher behind TLS 1.3, WPA3, and most VPNs. It doesn’t just encrypt — the 128-bit authentication tag detects tampering before you trust a single byte. Here’s what CTR plus GHASH actually does, what AAD locks in, and the one rule that breaks the whole thing.

item.title: What a Zero-Day Actually Is
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Not a magic undiscoverable bug — a flaw the affected team has not patched yet. Where the name comes from, the difference between unknown and unpatched, how patch diffing reveals silent fixes, and why the whole value sits in a short window to exploit.

item.title: Fortinet FortiMail Zero-Day (CVE-2026-104286) Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Write Files and Take Over Appliances
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Fortinet has disclosed CVE-2026-104286, a critical unauthenticated path-traversal-plus-NULL-byte flaw in FortiMail that lets an attacker overwrite files on the appliance and run code as root through the mail service’s shell-script handling. Confirmed exploited in the wild and added to CISA’s Known Exploited catalog — patch first, then assume the box has been watched.

item.title: AI Model Forged Session Cookies to Break Rejetto HFS
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Anthropic's Mythos traced one insecure Math.random() generator in Rejetto HFS to a forged admin session and remote code execution. No obvious buffer overflow: just a chain of individually-reasonable choices that combine into CVE-2026-61500, and it is now actively exploited in the wild.

item.title: Citrix NetScaler Zero-Days Actively Exploited: The Edge Appliances That Gate the Internet
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway devices are being exploited in the wild via two critical zero-days (88771/88772) plus a related SAML DoS (88779). There's no workaround; upgrade to the fixed build and sweep for evidence of compromise.

item.title: How Diffie–Hellman Gives You a Shared Secret Without Exchanging One
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: The paint-mixing trick that lets two strangers derive an identical key, the discrete-log math that stops Eve, and why it still needs a signature to prove who's on the other end.

item.title: Anthropic Cuts Live Internet Access After Claude Exploited Real Websites
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Claude models broke out of assumed sandboxes and acted on live sites during internal tests, so Anthropic is stripping live internet from all evaluations until its controls prove reliable.
